summary: Eldorado NF stone-and-wood lookout west of Lake Tahoe: cab station by 1932, stone tower 1939-1942, cab 1949, 2024 HistoriCorps repairs. Rental status unconfirmed.

facts.design: 20-foot stone live-in tower topped with a 14 by 14 foot wooden observation cab; designed by Region 5 architect Kepler Johnson (HistoriCorps)

access.note: Road gated quite a way from the lookout (2006 visit report). Campflare lists the site as Closed, says it does not appear on Recreation.gov, and expected a 2025 rental opening. No confirmed opening found.

visit.trail_note: 2006 visit report: road gated quite a way from the lookout. Campflare lists the site as Closed; check with Eldorado National Forest before planning a visit.

events.note: Forest Service survey for a road to the top of Bunker Hill; lookout to be established once the road is built
Joe Baumann was the lookout at Bunker Hill Lookout Station; he fell from the roof in July 1932 and Raymond Lawyer and Gus Kyburz substituted
Construction began under Eldorado NF with CCC help, designed by Region 5 architect Kepler Johnson
Stone tower base finished (HistoriCorps); NHLR gives 1942 as build year by Joe Bauman
Baumanns finished the stone work through 1945
Wooden observation cab added on top of the stone tower
NHLR registration date September 21, 2004 as US 593, CA 64
NHLR visit report (Sept 30, 2006): looks manned seasonally, road gated, three antennas suggest a repeater site
FFLA restoration grant to the site; purpose and amount not stated. An unused $9.38 was returned (reported in the 2018 annual report)
HistoriCorps volunteer restoration: roof repair and replacement, brick chimney removal, water damage repairs, prep for repointing and paint. Campflare says completed in 2024.

corrections.proposed: Construction began 1939 (design by Kepler Johnson); stone base finished by 1942; wooden observation cab added 1949; a lookout station was staffed by 1932
corrections.why: The record gives only the 1942 NHLR build date. HistoriCorps dates the start to 1939 and the wooden cab to 1949, and a 1932 newspaper item shows an earlier station in use.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says Joe Bauman built it in 1942. HistoriCorps says construction began in 1939, the stone base was finished by 1942 and the cab was added in 1949. Campflare says it was constructed between 1942 and 1949. The story reports 1939 to 1949 with 1942 as the NHLR build year.

Sources spell the builder Bauman (NHLR, Campflare), Baumann (HistoriCorps, Forest Lookouts), and Joe Baumann in 1932. The story uses Joe Baumann for the 1932 keeper and Joe Bauman where the NHLR names the builder.

NHLR says it was one of three sites selected to receive this special stone tower; Campflare says it is one of only three such structures in California's national forests. HistoriCorps says the lookout is the only structure of its kind. The story follows the NHLR and Campflare wording.
NHLR gives 7,502 ft (2,287 m). Campflare gives approximately 7,524 ft. The record's 2286.6 m follows NHLR.

HistoriCorps lists repointing and paint as prep work to follow the roof and chimney. Campflare says the 2024 work included masonry repointing. The story says repointing and paint were to follow and attributes the completion claim to Campflare.

notes_for_editor: Rental status unconfirmed: Campflare shows the site as Closed and says a 2025 rental was anticipated but not on Recreation.gov; a Roamze listing repeats the 2025 expectation. Did not verify the brief's 2017 $500 FFLA grant; the 2018 report mentions only the 2016 grant to this site. The 2016 grant amount is not stated in sources read. Two WebSearch calls used (budget met). A lookout station was staffed in 1932, before the stone tower's 1942 build year in the record; the story presents the station and the tower as separate stages.
